*   **Strengths:** Compact memory footprint; supports non-power-of-two dimensions; supports heterogeneous materials; suitable for real-time visualization and geological operations (slicing, layer attenuation) [S1].

The evidence explicitly supports all points in the claim: 1) 'Compact memory footprint' is supported by comparisons showing SBRT uses significantly less memory than voxel and octree models (e.g., 2.628 MB vs 61.035 MB). 2) 'Supports non-power-of-two dimensions' is supported by the statement that SBRT does not have the constraint of octrees requiring power-of-two padding. 3) 'Supports heterogeneous materials' is supported by the text stating that hierarchical structures do not adequately support material mixing/heterogeneous materials, whereas SBRT handles this more simply. 4) 'Suitable for real-time visualization and geological operations (slicing, layer attenuation)' is supported by the description of the method allowing real-time visualization and operations such as 'cortes transversales' (slicing) and 'atenuación de capas' (layer attenuation).
supported

Stack-Based Terrain Representation (SBRT) is a compact 3D data structure that generalizes heightmaps by storing a vertical sequence of intervals for each $(x,y)$ coordinate, where each interval consists of a start height and an attribute (e.g., material type) [S1].

The claim states that SBRT is a compact 3D data structure generalizing heightmaps by storing a vertical sequence of intervals (start height and attribute) for each (x,y) coordinate. Source [S1] explicitly confirms this in the passages: 'e puede considerar como una generalización de los mapas de altura... la SBRT almacena un conjunto de intervalos. Cada uno está formado por una altura inicial y un atributo' (can be considered a generalization of heightmaps... SBRT stores a set of intervals. Each is formed by an initial height and an attribute). The source also describes it as a 'compacta' (compact) structure and notes it solves issues with voxel memory footprints, supporting the 'compact 3D data structure' aspect.
supported

The passage from Source [S1] explicitly states: 'Los resultados muestran cómo la SBRT tiene un consumo de memoria claramente menor que los otros métodos: inferior al 10 % del de un modelo de vóxel equivalente y entre un 13 % y un 30 % del requerido por un octree.' supported
It is particularly suited for modeling subsurface data obtained from geological boreholes (catas) and interpolated layer models [S1].

The claim states that the method is particularly suited for modeling subsurface data from geological boreholes (catas) and interpolated layer models. Source [S1] explicitly states in the passages: 'Además de para codificar terrenos volumétricos, esta representación es ideal para modelar un conjunto de datos obtenidos a partir de catas geológicas.' (In addition to encoding volumetric terrains, this representation is ideal for modeling a set of data obtained from geological boreholes.) It further explains that a common way to obtain a subsurface model from boreholes is through interpolation/extrapolation resulting in a layer model ('modelo por capas'), and that a stack-based terrain representation fits this type of model perfectly ('Una representación de terrenos basada en stacks se ajusta a la perfección a este tipo de modelos'). Therefore, every fact in the claim is supported by the evidence.
